title: Towards Responsible Development of Generative AI for Education: An Evaluation-Driven Approach
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to responsibly develop and evaluate generative AI systems for education, especially conversational tutoring systems. The authors argue that progress has been slowed by a lack of clear pedagogical goals, weak evaluation practices, and difficulty translating learning-science principles into machine-readable prompts or training data.

The paper presents an evaluation-driven development approach for LearnLM-Tutor, a text-based gen AI tutor built on Gemini 1.0. The intervention includes participatory design with learners and educators, workshops, interviews, Wizard-of-Oz sessions, and co-design activities to derive pedagogical principles such as encouraging active learning, managing cognitive load, supporting metacognition, motivating curiosity, and adapting to learner needs. These principles were then used to create fine-tuning datasets and seven evaluation benchmarks spanning automatic and human assessment.

The empirical context includes university students, adult coding learners, high school STEM teachers, and educators/researchers involved in participatory studies and evaluation. The paper concludes that fine-tuning and targeted pedagogical datasets improve LearnLM-Tutor relative to prompt-tuned Gemini on multiple pedagogical dimensions, while emphasizing that evaluation of AI tutors should go beyond accuracy to include pedagogy, safety, learner feedback, and real-world deployment considerations.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a technical/report-style paper focused on model development and evaluation benchmarks rather than a controlled educational efficacy study. It includes human preference and turn-level evaluations, but not a well-designed RCT or QED measuring learner outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports pedagogical preference and benchmark improvements for an LLM tutor, but does not provide direct evidence of medium or large effects on learning outcomes. Its impact is promising yet indirect, with no demonstrated causal effect on student achievement or broader institutional outcomes.

interventions.use_case: Text-based generative AI tutor (LearnLM-Tutor) for 1:1 conversational tutoring, including grounded explanations, step-by-step guidance, hints, checking understanding, and pedagogical feedback for learners.
